title: Ephemeral Environments: Cost Controls, RBAC, and Lifecycle Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook documents the standard process for provisioning, governing, and retiring ephemeral environments (dev/test/feature-preview) intended for platform and product teams. Focus areas: cost containment, role-based access controls (RBAC), observability onboarding, automated TTL lifecycle, and post-mortem templates for environment incidents.

Goals
-----
- Keep per-environment monthly cost under $200 for single-node GPUless environments and under $1,500 for multi-node GPU previews unless explicitly approved.
- Enforce least-privilege access by default; require approval for write-level network or KMS access.
- Reduce orphaned ephemeral environments >72 hours by 90% within three months via automation and alerting.
- Provide a reproducible teardown process and clear ownership for each environment.

When to use this playbook
-------------------------
Use for: feature branch previews, demo environments, partner staging, customer PoC sandboxes. Do NOT use for: production replicas handling live data, long-running performance experiments without prior capacity sign-off.

Key concepts and vocabulary
---------------------------
- Ephemeral environment: short-lived environment spun up automatically from PRs or by CLI; expected TTL = 24–72 hours.
- Owner tag: metadata identifying a primary owner (team and oncall) that appears in dashboards. Format: owner:team/name@redwood.com.
- Cost cap: a soft limit (monthly estimate) enforced via budget policies and throttling.
- Preview role: RBAC profile with read-only infra network + limited secret access.

Owner and escalation
--------------------
- Primary owner: Platform Environments (eng-platform) — rotation lead: Maya Chen (primary) / Liam O'Connor (backup).
- Escalation path: Environment owner -> Platform oncall -> Infra SRE lead -> CTO operations if >8 hours outage impacting demos.

Provisioning checklist (automated CI flow)
-----------------------------------------
1. PR triggers pipeline: runs IaC plan (Terragrunt/Terraform) in a sandbox workspace.
2. Create ephemeral namespace with labels: project, pr-id, owner, cost-center.
3. Apply a Preview role binding (Kubernetes RBAC) limiting access to: get/list/describe for core infra, no cluster-admin.
4. Inject secrets via ephemeral secret store scoped to preview role (no KMS unwrapping).
5. Deploy observability sidecars: tracing and metrics exporters are mandatory.
6. Run smoke healthcheck and register environment in Ephemeral Registry service.
7. Assign TTL and schedule automatic teardown.

RBAC profile (recommended)
-------------------------
- preview-role (k8s ClusterRole):
  - allowed: get, list, watch for Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets (read-only); exec into pods disabled.
  - denied: create/patch/delete on node/cluster-resources, no persistentVolumeClaims by default.
- admin-preview (approval required):
  - allowed: elevated service account for operations teams; requires a JIRA ticket and time-bounded grant (max 48 hours).

Example Kubernetes YAML snippet
------------------------------
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: preview-rolebinding-pr-1234
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: preview-runner
  namespace: preview-pr-1234
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: preview-role
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io

Cost controls and enforcement
-----------------------------
- Default machine types: t3.medium-equivalent for app nodes; g4dn.xlarge disallowed unless GPU-request approved.
- Quotas: Ephemeral Registry enforces a per-team concurrent environment quota (default 5).
- Budget trigger: Cloud billing alert when estimated monthly cost > 85% of cost cap; triggers environment suspension (read-only) and notifies owner.
- Auto-throttle policy: scale replicas to 1 and reduce CPU to 200m when idle metric <5% CPU for 15m.

Monitoring, dashboards, and alerts
----------------------------------
Dashboards (must be auto-created at provision):
- Ephemeral Overview: shows active envs, owner, ttl, estimated hourly cost.
- Cost by PR: chargeback view grouped by repo and team.
- Health Summary: error rate, latency P95 for preview APIs.

Alert thresholds (examples)
- Orphaned env (>72h without latest commit): p1 alert to platform-owner mailing list.
- Cost spike (env hourly >3x baseline for 30m): p2 alert to owner and SRE.
- Observability missing (no traces for 10m): p2 alert and auto-tag env as degraded.

Runbook: immediate actions for a cost spike
-----------------------------------------
1. Identify environment from dashboard -> click into Ephemeral Registry.
2. Check owner tag and notify via Slack (#platform-ephemeral).
3. If spike is benign (load test), acknowledge and document run in registry.
4. If spike is unexpected: scale down replicas, restrict external ingress, and snapshot logs.
5. If cost exceeds 200% of expected for 1h, suspend environment and open a JIRA with label "ephemeral-cost-incident".

Automated TTL lifecycle policy (implementation notes)
----------------------------------------------------
- When created, env gets TTL metadata: created_at, expires_at. A cleanup controller runs every 15 minutes and:
  - If expires_at < now -> mark for termination and send pre-termination notice 30 minutes prior.
  - If marked 'extended' -> evaluate remaining budget; extensions require owner approval via Jira API.

API examples
------------
- Create preview (CLI):
  redwood preview create --repo infra/repo --pr 1234 --owner "team/backend/alex@redwood.com" --ttl 48h
- Extend preview (via API):
  POST /api/v1/previews/1234/extend {"owner":"alex@redwood.com","hours":24}

Chargeback and tagging rules
---------------------------
- Tagging format: repo:team:pr (e.g., agent-service:payments:2345). Billing pipeline aggregates tags hourly.
- Teams with recurring high spend (>10 env-hours/day avg) get notified monthly with optimization recommendations.

Security hardening checklist (must pass before public partner previews)
---------------------------------------------------------------------
- No production dataset mounts.
- Secrets are read-only and ephemeral; rotate service tokens every 24h.
- Private network endpoints require approval and documented justification.
- Penetration checklist: static-scan, dependency-scan, credentials-scan passed.

Post-incident retrospective template for environment outages
-----------------------------------------------------------
1. Incident summary (one-liner)
2. Timeline (UTC)
3. Impacted envs and owners
4. Root cause analysis (technical + process)
5. Corrective actions and owners (with due dates)
6. Metrics to monitor and SLO changes (if any)
7. Retro notes and follow-up meeting date

Retro example (brief)
--------------------
- Incident: Excessive egress billing from preview-pr-839 on 2026-01-21.
- Root cause: A misconfigured data sink in third-party integration created a background job.
- Fix: Added network egress policy, revoked third-party token, added smoke test.
- Action items: ticket #PLAT-342 (owner: Priya Menon, due: 2026-02-02).

Roadmap and improvements (Q1–Q3 2026)
-------------------------------------
- Q1: Implement quota-aware preflight checks in CI pipelines.
- Q2: Add budget-aware autoscaling rules integrated with billing metrics.
- Q3: Fine-grained RBAC self-serve granting interface with audit trail.

Appendices
---------
A. Failure-mode matrix (short)
- Missing TTL: Orphaned envs -> remediations: alert + automated termination.
- Secret leakage risk: Immediate revoke + audit, rotate relevant tokens.
- High cost from external traffic: throttle ingress + block egress to unapproved endpoints.

B. Quick commands
- List previews: redwood preview list --team payments
- Force terminate: redwood preview terminate --id preview-pr-1234 --reason "cost spike"
